phases.name: verification
phases.note: Debug APK rebuilt after both rounds. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the first two builds (BUILD SUCCESSFUL) were misleading -- standard RN debug builds do NOT bundle JS into the APK (confirmed via build.gradle's own comment: debug variant skips the JS-bundling task by default), meaning a sideloaded debug APK without a running Metro server would show a 'could not connect to development server' error instead of any of the fixes. Corrected by manually running `npx react-native bundle --dev false` and placing the output at android/app/src/main/assets/index.android.bundle before the final rebuild, so the APK is self-contained and installable without Metro. Output: android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk (450MB, built 2026-10-12 12:04). CONFIRMED via `unzip -l` that assets/index.android.bundle (18.5MB) is genuinely packaged inside -- this is a real, self-contained APK, not a Metro-dependent one. No physical device connected yet -- `adb devices` empty as of last check; user is sideloading the file directly instead. This is source-level verification (typecheck+build+self-contained-bundle-confirmed) -- actual on-device behavioral verification still pending the user's physical-device test.

screen_audit_batches.name: church_family

MOST SEVERE FINDING OF THE ENTIRE SESSION, independently and thoroughly verified via full git diff: src/screens/family/SOSScreen.tsx (the actual family-emergency SOS button) called setSent(true) -- showing 'Alert Sent - Help is on the way' -- unconditionally as soon as the network call did not THROW, completely ignoring whether the backend actually accepted the SOS (postRequest resolves successfully even on a rejected/failed request, per the repeatedly-confirmed behavior of this codebase's network layer all session). Uneven loading/error/empty-state coverage is the norm, not the exception, across almost every domain batch.
